conventions.axes: Same world as v4-spec.json: metres, origin on the living-room floor at its back wall, X right as the living master camera sees it, Y from the living back wall toward the entrance, Z up. All room rectangles are INTERIOR wall faces.
conventions.compass: north = -X, south = +X, east = -Y, west = +Y. Plan drawing: -Y (east) up, -X (north) left.
conventions.yaw_deg_left: As v4-spec: heading from -Y, positive toward -X. f = (-sin yaw, -cos yaw), r = (cos yaw, -sin yaw).
conventions.projection: d = f.(P-C), x = r.(P-C); u = u0 + 0.6667 x/d; v = v0 + 1.1852 (Hc - Z)/d (24 mm, 16:9). Hc = camera height of that frame (1.1; was 1.20 everywhere). Floor visible from depth d >= 1.1852 Hc / (1 - v0).
conventions.walls: Interior partitions 0.15. Exterior walls 0.35 everywhere, including around the entrance court. Documented exceptions: see 'documented_walls'.
conventions.sun: Render time 15:00 mid-winter for the whole house (Bible 1.4). Every window seen in, or lighting, a master frame is on a north or east facade (in shade at that hour); 1.1: or an opal roof light (hall, corridor; diffuse, no sun patch). South/west walls in frames are solid.
conventions.transition_grammar: motion-direction 2.3 + U4 + U5 + U20: each shot is one straight move with constant heading (dolly forward, pull-back, slider, pedestal, merged into one vector; may be oblique to the heading) or a pan-only shot of <= 35 deg from a fixed point. 1.1: a slider may cross a doorway (>= 0.15 to the jambs); the camera height change of an arrival is merged into its last straight vector; two frames of one room are linked by one in-room pan (P-B, P-D). Playback per U10.

fillers_rule.rule: Every standalone object in any frame is a sellable product (a slot with a product card). Only 'fillers' may be unsold: contents that show a sold product in use (candles in the candle holders, plant in the planter, magazines in the holder, stems in a vase). A filler is identical in all 3 variations of its slot, never in the cart, and the product page says it is not included. Anything else that is not a product stays out of frame. Fixed furniture and shell (sofa, tables, chairs, beds, cabinets, sanitary ware, the bath mirror per U6) are neither fillers nor products.

keys in the key tray (tray stays empty)
laptop, papers and stationery on the desks (pencils in the organizer are a filler)
toys that are not a product slot (kids: soft-toy, toy-cars, skateboard, doll, doll-pram are products)

open_1_1: Counting rule for S11 (Bible 1.6): the proposal's 0.5% area threshold counted only 1-8 products in the frames the user approved (small tabletop items at 3-4 m). 1.1 counts a product that is >= 0.1% of the frame and >= 50% visible, or a decisively cut large textile whose visible part is >= 1% of the frame; a set counts once if one piece qualifies. With it every frame meets its minimum. Confirm.

Designer additions made under the 2026-10-08 density decision, not visible in the approved clay: hall storage-boxes and bench-throw (and the basket moved to the bench's corner end); corridor gallery-stool (runner narrowed to 60, optional picture-ledge dropped); work desk-organizer; master bedside-carafe, sill-vase, trinket-dish; kitchen step-stool. Each is the first to go if the mock-up reads busy.

Transit-only products (not in any master frame, so not tappable there): hall runner-rug and ceiling-light, master rug, basket and pendant, bath ceiling-light. Keep them as products (seen in the transitions and the corridor vista) or drop them.
